key_insight: Wonder turns a single image or conditional video into a playable, real-time world model that users can explore by moving the camera. Its core advance is co-designing control, memory, and training so the model can revisit known areas and discover unseen regions over long horizons.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of building a general-purpose video world model that is both interactive and temporally consistent, while supporting real-time camera control and long-term exploration.
method: Builds a camera-controllable video world model from an image or conditional video input.
Uses a system-level co-design of control mechanisms, memory for preserving past observations, and training strategy for stable long-horizon generation.
Supports interactive navigation in a playable environment, enabling users to explore unseen regions and return to previously viewed areas in real time.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, Wonder provides a practical step toward interactive generative environments for simulation, planning, and content creation. It highlights how combining control, memory, and training design can improve realism and consistency in world models.

paper_title: Wonder: Video World Model Done Better
paper_authors: Jiacong Xu, Hanwen Jiang, Zhixin Shu, Kalyan Sunkavalli, Vishal M. Patel
